answer: Make every identity pay a real compute cost before it can join. To register, an agent must solve a proof-of-work puzzle bound to its public key, like carving its name into basalt: trivial for one honest agent, but an attacker minting ten thousand fakes must burn a data center's worth of electricity and hardware time. The kernel of the defense is asymmetry — the work is cheap to verify and expensive to repeat at scale. A mesa of fake accounts collapses under its own weight, because each extra identity costs the attacker real resources while a legitimate agent pays only once.
